title: The Levelled Disc
logline: A clay-worker levels a plain reddish disc for a lay meditation class down the road, smoothing it again each time the sun cracks it, while a whole village day organises itself around one small, deliberately uninteresting object.
human_question: What can a person do with attention that has nowhere interesting to land?

premise.story: A potter or clay-worker prepares kasiṇa discs for a nearby lay meditation teacher: sourcing the right clay, kneading out grit, levelling the surface like a drum skin, re-levelling it each time it dries and cracks, and finally delivering finished discs to the hall.
premise.place: A small clay-working household in a dry-zone or low-country pottery village, and the plain lay meditation hall it supplies.
premise.experience: The hypnotic patience of getting one small circle of clay perfectly flat and dull, and the discovery that the whole discipline of stillness can begin with something this ordinary.

concept_links.why: Kasiṇa practice begins with exactly this act of craft: a disc of smooth reddish clay, made and re-levelled until it is as even as a drum face, then used as a training object for attention [C087-P4:L209; C087-M:L19–L21].

The sources describe deep concentration through the same image of bringing an object close and looking long at its colour and marks until it is completely clear; the finished disc is what such attention would eventually rest on [C013-P:L48–L52].
The disc is one of forty listed meditation subjects, chosen to fit different temperaments; the film can show it made without explaining the larger list.

what_camera_could_observe: Picking grit and stones out of wet clay, testing it between the fingers
The board or palm smoothing the surface, cracks appearing as it dries in the sun, the patient re-levelling
The finished discs stacked, wrapped and carried to the hall on a bicycle or in a basket
A brief, unexplained glimpse of the hall itself: mats, low light, a few people already seated
what_must_be_real: The clay-worker's actual livelihood, orders and relationship with the meditation hall. No one performs meditation for the camera, and the clay-worker is not shown as practising.

possible_arc.opening: Grit picked from wet clay, an ordinary morning's work.
possible_arc.turn: A disc cracks in the sun and has to be redone; the deadline for delivery presses.
possible_arc.ending_open: The discs are carried to the hall and set down. Whether Chathura is given one, and by whom, is for reality to decide.

position_hint: opening candidate: a plausible, ordinary place for Object 10 to be acquired if a disc, or the clay-worker's own tool, is genuinely given to Chathura; the object fits the group's hint of 'something that helps stillness.'

requirements: A working clay craftsperson supplying a real meditation hall or teacher
Consent to film both the workshop and, briefly and respectfully, the exterior of the hall
A finished disc or delivery to follow during the filming window

suggestions.name: Molagoda pottery village
suggestions.why: A traditional clay-working area in the low country.
suggestions.verify: Whether kasiṇa discs specifically are made to order there, or only domestic pottery, is unverified.

risks: Turning craft into pure metaphor with no livelihood at stake
Implying the clay-worker practises kasiṇa themselves without evidence
The link to meditation could feel imposed if no real hall or teacher is found
drop_if: No clay-worker can be found who actually supplies discs to a real, willing meditation teacher or hall

connections.note: Both look at the plain, made objects a meditator's attention rests on, from opposite ends: making one object closely, and choosing among forty.
A different, non-craft way Object 10 could be acquired at the group's opening.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
